subject: sci
source: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science (0653) syllabus for examination in 2028 and 2029 (topics B1–B16, C1–C12, P1–P5) — Cambridge International; Year 10 rotates biology, chemistry and physics through the first half of the course

weeks.topic: Biology: characteristics of living organisms
objectives: Describe the seven characteristics of living organisms
Apply them to decide whether something is alive

weeks.topic: Chemistry: solids, liquids, gases and changes of state
objectives: Describe particle arrangement and motion in each state
Explain changes of state using particle theory

weeks.topic: Physics: physical quantities, measurement and speed
objectives: Measure length, volume and time accurately
Calculate speed and average speed

weeks.topic: Biology: cell structure and size of specimens
objectives: Identify structures in animal and plant cells and their functions
Use magnification = image size / actual size

weeks.topic: Chemistry: elements, compounds and mixtures
objectives: Distinguish elements, compounds and mixtures
Compare metals and non-metals

weeks.topic: Physics: speed–time graphs and acceleration
objectives: Sketch and interpret distance–time and speed–time graphs
Calculate acceleration and distance travelled

weeks.topic: Biology: diffusion, osmosis and active transport
objectives: Define diffusion, osmosis and active transport
Investigate osmosis in plant tissue

weeks.topic: Chemistry: atomic structure and the Periodic Table
objectives: Describe protons, neutrons and electrons
Write electronic configurations
Relate configuration to group and period

weeks.topic: Physics: mass, weight and density
objectives: Distinguish mass and weight using W = mg
Calculate density and measure it for solids and liquids

weeks.topic: Biology: biological molecules and food tests
objectives: Name the building blocks of carbohydrates, fats and proteins
Carry out food tests for starch, sugars, proteins and fats

weeks.topic: Chemistry: ions and ionic bonds
objectives: Describe ion formation by electron transfer
Draw dot-and-cross diagrams for ionic compounds
Relate ionic structure to properties

weeks.topic: Physics: effects of forces and load–extension graphs
objectives: Describe how forces change speed, direction and shape
Find resultant forces
Interpret load–extension graphs

weeks.topic: Biology: enzymes
objectives: Explain enzymes as biological catalysts
Investigate the effects of temperature and pH on enzyme activity

weeks.topic: Chemistry: simple molecules and covalent bonds
objectives: Describe covalent bonding as shared electron pairs
Draw dot-and-cross diagrams for simple molecules
Explain properties of simple molecular substances

weeks.topic: Review: living organisms, cells, particles, atoms, bonding and motion
objectives: Revisit key biology, chemistry and physics definitions
Practise mixed-science short-answer questions

weeks.topic: Physics: energy stores, transfers and work done
objectives: Identify energy stores and transfers
Apply conservation of energy
Calculate work done = force × distance

weeks.topic: Biology: photosynthesis and leaf structure
objectives: State the word equation for photosynthesis
Investigate limiting factors
Relate leaf structure to photosynthesis

weeks.topic: Chemistry: formulas, word and symbol equations
objectives: Write formulae of simple compounds
Write and balance symbol equations with state symbols

weeks.topic: Physics: energy resources and power
objectives: Compare renewable and non-renewable energy resources
Calculate power as energy transferred per second

weeks.topic: Biology: human nutrition and a balanced diet
objectives: Describe the components of a balanced diet
Explain causes of deficiency diseases

weeks.topic: Biology: the digestive system and digestion
objectives: Identify organs of the digestive system
Describe physical and chemical digestion by amylase, protease and lipase

weeks.topic: Chemistry: electrolysis
objectives: Describe electrolysis of molten and aqueous compounds
Predict products at the anode and cathode

weeks.topic: Physics: pressure
objectives: Use pressure = force / area
Explain everyday applications of high and low pressure

weeks.topic: Chemistry: exothermic and endothermic reactions
objectives: Define exothermic and endothermic reactions
Interpret reaction pathway diagrams

weeks.topic: Biology: transport in plants — xylem, phloem and transpiration
objectives: Identify xylem and phloem
Describe water uptake and transpiration
Investigate factors affecting transpiration rate

weeks.topic: Chemistry: physical and chemical changes and rate of reaction
objectives: Distinguish physical and chemical changes
Investigate factors affecting rate of reaction
Explain rates using collision theory

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: biology, chemistry and physics content taught so far
objectives: Complete timed mixed-science papers
Identify weak topics in each science

weeks.topic: Physics: kinetic particle model and pressure changes in gases
objectives: Describe particle arrangement in the three states
Explain gas pressure changes with temperature and volume

weeks.topic: Biology: the circulatory system, heart and blood vessels
objectives: Describe the double circulation and heart structure
Relate the structure of arteries, veins and capillaries to function

weeks.topic: Chemistry: redox reactions
objectives: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of oxygen gain and loss
Identify redox in simple reactions

weeks.topic: Physics: thermal expansion and evaporation
objectives: Describe thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases
Explain cooling by evaporation

weeks.topic: Biology: blood
objectives: Identify components of blood and their functions
Describe the roles of phagocytes and lymphocytes

weeks.topic: Chemistry: properties of acids and bases; oxides
objectives: Describe reactions of acids with metals, bases and carbonates
Use the pH scale and indicators
Classify oxides as acidic or basic

weeks.topic: Physics: conduction, convection and radiation
objectives: Explain thermal energy transfer by conduction, convection and radiation
Describe everyday consequences and applications

weeks.topic: Biology: diseases and immunity
objectives: Describe pathogens and how diseases spread
Explain body defences, antibodies and vaccination

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: all Year 10 combined science content
objectives: Complete end-of-year papers across all three sciences
Apply data-handling skills to unfamiliar contexts

weeks.topic: Review: nutrition, transport, reactions, acids and thermal physics
objectives: Correct errors from end-of-year exams
Consolidate key equations and definitions
